subject: Pool headroom eviction spike — runbook, mitigation, and credit offer
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
To: Nimbus Health Ops <ops@nimbushealth.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 16:14:00 -0800
Subject: Pool headroom eviction spike — runbook, mitigation, and credit offer

Hi Elena / Nimbus Ops team,

TL;DR: Between 15:42–15:54 PST today one of the Dedicated GPU pools serving your NB-4921 reserved nodes experienced a headroom drop that triggered an eviction spike for long-running KV-cache-heavy requests. We applied a temporary traffic throttle and rebalanced two nodes to reduce evictions; you may see a short blip in 95th pct latency during that window.

What happened (summary):
- Around 15:42 a model rollout with higher memory pressure combined with a traffic burst from a nightly batch caused pool headroom to fall below our safety threshold.
- The autoscaler kicked a scale-down action (incorrectly delayed), and the eviction controller began reclaiming KV segments to free memory, which led to ~120 eviction events that impacted 8 of your active sessions.

Immediate mitigations we performed:
- Re-enabled conservative autoscaler hold (15:50) to prevent further unintended scale decisions.
- Shuffled two reserved nodes out of the affected pool and drained them; moved the tenant slots for NB-4921 to warmed nodes (15:58).
- Applied a per-tenant short-term throttle (1 minute window) to smooth the burst and avoid repeated cache thrashing.

Attachments: I attached a short runbook (runbook_eviction_mitigation.pdf) and raw logs we collected (log_export_20270202.zip). The ops log includes the eviction trace and autoscaler signals.

Ask from you: Can you confirm the endpoints that saw errors during 15:42–16:00 PST and whether you saw any user-facing retries? That will help us map impact to API routes.

I'll follow up with a post-incident runbook and a one-time service credit for the disrupted window. We've prioritized a fix in the autoscaler hold logic (SUP-921).

Sorry for the disruption — we know this is sensitive for you. I'm available for a quick sync if you'd like to walk the timeline together.

Regards,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbushealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>, Nimbus Health Ops <ops@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 17:03:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Pool headroom eviction spike — runbook, mitigation, and credit offer

Thanks Avery — appreciate the quick update and the artifacts.

Impact for us: The /patient-summary and /billing/charge endpoints returned 503 for several requests between 15:43 and 15:49 PST; we saw client-side retries that surfaced to some dashboards. We believe roughly 0.6% of API calls during that hour failed (sampling). Latency returned to normal after 15:59.

Questions:
1) Do you have a preliminary root cause (autoscaler delay vs rollout memory regression)?
2) Will the throttle affect throughput for any sustained production traffic windows tomorrow morning (we have a scheduled job at 06:00 PST)?

We'd like a short call to confirm the runbook and confirm the scope of the credit. I'm available tomorrow 08:30–10:00 PST.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Reliability, Nimbus Health
elena@nimbushealth.com

From: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 18:11:05 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Pool headroom eviction spike — runbook, mitigation, and credit offer

Marissa / David / Monica — looping you in. Elena asked for preliminary root cause and impact details; attaching logs. Key actions we need today:

1) Tech root cause & short writeup (owner: David) — confirm whether the autoscaler hold race or rollout memory delta was primary. Include evidence from heap/KV metrics.
2) Runbook confirmation (owner: Monica) — ensure the attached runbook_eviction_mitigation.pdf has precise operator steps we executed and clear rollback instructions. Add a step for pre-rollout memory dry-run for Dedicated pools.
3) Customer comms + credit proposal (owner: Marissa) — propose a one-time credit covering the affected 18-minute window; Elena asked about scope. Draft language and a credit note (pdf) we can attach.

Notes from logs (quick):
- Eviction spike timestamps: 2027-02-02T15:42:31–2027-02-02T15:54:12 PST.
- Autoscaler signaled "scale_down" twice at 15:46 but the hold handler ignored the warmup flag because of a concurrent rollout tag.
- Several KV segments were evicted for sessions with >2x sequence length compared to baseline.

Attached: log_export_20270202.zip. I asked Elena to confirm endpoints; she reported /patient-summary and /billing/charge.

David — can you prioritise SUP-921 postmortem notes tonight so we can share preliminary root cause in the morning? Marissa / Monica — aim to have draft credit language and runbook updates by 09:00 PST tomorrow so I can share with the customer in the 08:30–09:00 slot if they confirm.

From: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimbushealth.com>, Nimbus Health Ops <ops@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident runbook, timeline, and one-time credit for NB-4921

Hi Elena — thanks again for the quick verification on impacted endpoints. Attached are three items: runbook_eviction_mitigation.pdf (ops runbook with changes highlighted), a condensed timeline and preliminary root cause notes, and credit_note_NB-4921.pdf (one-time service credit covering the affected window).

Condensed timeline (finalized):
- 15:42:31 PST — memory pressure increased during model variant rollout; pool headroom crossed warning threshold.
- 15:46:05 PST — autoscaler emitted scale_down signals; a concurrent rollout tag prevented the autoscaler hold from taking effect.
- 15:47:10–15:54:12 PST — eviction controller reclaimed KV segments, causing transient 503s on several endpoints.
- 15:58:00 PST — ops rebalanced two warm nodes and applied per-tenant smoothing throttle.
- 15:59:30 PST — 95th pct latency returned to baseline.

Preliminary root cause (summary):
- Primary cause: autoscaler hold race condition during concurrent rollout (we're tracking a patch under SUP-921).
- Contributing factor: model variant introduced higher memory working set for long-context requests without a dedicated pre-warm step.

Runbook changes included:
- Add explicit pre-rollout memory dry-run to Dedicated pools for any model variant that increases KV usage.
- Ensure autoscaler hold respects rollout tags when warmup flags are present (patch planned; will ship in next deployment window).
- Telemetry: new alert for sustained headroom decline for >60s without scale action.

Customer compensation: We propose a one-time credit equal to the pro-rated usage during 15:42–15:59 PST for account NB-4921. Credit details are in the attached credit_note_NB-4921.pdf. If that is acceptable we will apply it to your next billing cycle.

Next steps / asks:
- Please confirm acceptance of the credit and whether you want a follow-up call (we're available 08:30–10:00 PST today).
- We'll schedule a technical review for SUP-921 with your SREs and our engineering team to walk the fix and preventive tests.

Again, apologies for the disruption. We're treating this as high priority and will share the full postmortem with root cause evidence and long-term mitigations by EOD Friday.

Regards,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery@redwood.com
